newsitem.title: FRANCE: Russian Communist leader satisfied by Chechen poll.
newsitem.headline: Russian Communist leader satisfied by Chechen poll.

text.p: Russian Communist leader Gennady Zyuganov expressed satisfaction on Tuesday with the expected victory in Chechnya's presidential elections of former rebel leader Aslan Maskhadov.

"He is a moderate and a military man who served in the Soviet army, and I believe he understands that Chechnya will never emerge from its crisis without Russia's help," Zyuganov told a news conference in Strasbourg, eastern France.
"I believe there will be a constructive dialogue with Chechnya and we are going to support it," said the Communist leader, who was defeated by Boris Yeltsin in Russian presidential elections in July.
Zyuganov was in Strasbourg in his role as a deputy in the 40-nation Council of Europe's parliamentary assembly.

Maskhadov, the rebel military chief who also led the Chechen delegation in last summer's peace talks with Moscow, is a staunch supporter of Chechen independence but has made clear he will seek better relations with Russia if elected president.
